description: What the Software Factory delivered and what it cost: tickets filed, PRs opened and merged, lead times, first-pass rate, Slack approvals, list-price spend, and modelled engineer-hours. Health and debugging are on Factory ops. Spend is a list-price estimate from token counts, not the invoice. Method on Factory ops.

options.content:
Turns Jira tickets into merged pull requests — plan, approve, build, review, merge — with people in the loop for approvals and merges.

**Read left to right:** delivery volume → quality and speed → spend. **Ticket pipeline** is the funnel (counts and reach rate). **Cost** uses list-price estimates, not the invoice — detail on Factory ops.

panels.description: Share of merges in the time range that needed no launch retry/heal and no Bugbot fix round. First pass means the ticket merged with no worker launch retry and no Bugbot fix round on its PR. Approximation: a Bugbot round that was granted but then failed still counts as a round (reads low); a PR the worker never tied to the ticket cannot be joined (reads high). Events that can predate the range (the filing, a launch retry, a Bugbot round) are counted over the dashboard range or the last 7 days, whichever is longer; older ones are missed.

panels.title: Engineer-hours saved

panels.description: How many tickets reached each stage in the time range, in pipeline order (Filed → Planned → Approved → PR opened → Merged). Each bar is distinct tickets that reached this stage **or any later one** — a later milestone implies the earlier stages (for example a PR opened without a logged approval still counts as Approved). The funnel only narrows. Tickets that entered the factory in the time range: the desk started watching as the ticket went to Triaged, or the planner started when that watch is missing. A ticket with no Slack thread and no plan is not counted, so this is an approximation that can read low.

defaults.noValue: No tickets in range. Widen the time range.

panels.title: Reach rate

panels.description: Filed → PR opened: filing to PR open. Filed → merged: filing to Done on a merged PR (includes review wait). One row per ticket; merged stays blank until Done. Per ticket, from filing to the first matching stage, using each ticket's own timestamps. Only tickets that reached the end stage in this range are measured; a ticket whose filing is older than the range or 7 days is left out. Tickets that entered the factory in the time range: the desk started watching as the ticket went to Triaged, or the planner started when that watch is missing. A ticket with no Slack thread and no plan is not counted, so this is an approximation that can read low.

panels.title: Cost by ticket

panels.description: Short note on what Spend measures.

options.content: Spend is **estimated** from token counts × Cursor list prices (not billing). **Cost by ticket** lists keyed tickets plus **Unattributed (before ticket tagging)** so the cost column sums to Spend. **Ticket flow** counts a later milestone as having reached every earlier stage (for example a PR without a logged approval still counts as Approved). Engineer-hours saved is a **model** (merged tickets × Hours / ticket). Full pricing assumptions live on [Factory ops](/d/factory-ops).

panels.title: About these figures

list.description: Hosted slug (resource service.name). All six factory slugs, idle ones included.
list.label: Service
list.name: service
list.query: factory-desk, factory-planner, factory-worker, factory-pr-autofixer, factory-security-reviewer, factory-triage-jira

list.description: MODELLED engineer-hours of manual work one merged ticket is assumed to replace: Engineer-hours saved (modelled) is merged tickets × this. The default 4 h is a conservative manual baseline for a small ticket (plan, implement, PR), not a measurement. Pick another value, or set var-hours_per_ticket in the URL.
list.label: Hours / ticket
list.name: hours_per_ticket

list.description: Width of each bar in the per-bucket panels. Prometheus widens the step on long ranges; Loki stays on this value. On a live range (to = now) the last bar is the in-progress bucket. Prometheus stops the last bar at the last whole ${prom_res} step at or before $__to (1m below 7d, 5m at 7d+) and keeps the bar that straddles $__from. A range end off that grid leaves up to one ${prom_res} step out of both the bars and the range stats; the two still agree. On a range that ends before now, a Loki last bar covers its whole bucket and can include up to one step after the range end. The first Loki bar starts at the first step boundary at or after the range start, so the left edge can show a gap.
list.label: Bucket
list.name: bucket

list.definition: query_result((label_replace(vector(1), "step", "5m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) >= 604800)) or (label_replace(vector(1), "step", "1m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) < 604800)))
list.description: Inner step of the Prometheus look-ahead and range subqueries. 1m below 7d (matches scrape); 5m at 7d+ for latency and query-cost (negative-offset subqueries are uncached). Measured on 20 token series: 30d 1m was 3.28s / 9.16M samples (peakSamples 475k) and 5m is 0.88s / 1.9M (peak 95k). Hidden; if the query fails Grafana keeps the JSON default 1m.
list.label: Prom subquery step
list.name: prom_res

query.query: query_result((label_replace(vector(1), "step", "5m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) >= 604800)) or (label_replace(vector(1), "step", "1m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) < 604800)))

list.definition: query_result((label_replace(vector(1), "smooth", "5m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) >= 604800)) or (label_replace(vector(1), "smooth", "2m", "", "") and on() (vector(${__to:date:seconds} - ${__from:date:seconds}) < 604800)))
list.description: Running-max window inside the Prometheus subquery for _total counters. 2m below 7d (hides multi-writer flips shorter than 2m); 5m at 7d+ so every ${prom_res} step sees the samples in that step. Hidden.
